To add 2/3 and 1/6, first find a common denominator. The least common multiple of 3 and 6 is 6. Convert 2/3 to a fraction with a denominator of 6: (2/3) × (2/2) = 4/6. Now add 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6. The sum of 2/3 and 1/6 is 5/6 [S1]. This process involves finding a common denominator and adjusting the fractions accordingly before adding them [S2]. This method ensures accuracy in fraction addition by aligning the denominators [S3]. Understanding how to find common denominators is crucial for adding fractions with different denominators [S4]. This approach is a fundamental skill in working with fractions, enabling precise calculations in various mathematical contexts [S5]. By converting fractions to equivalent forms with a common denominator, one can accurately perform addition and maintain the integrity of the numerical values [S6]. This method of adding fractions is a fundamental aspect of arithmetic, essential for solving problems involving multiple fractional terms [S7]. It highlights the importance of understanding common denominators in working with fractions [S8].
